description:
FILED s473t5f (#1501 round 7, uni/, 2026-09-13).  PRE-EXISTING; ASCII-probed,
so it is not a Unicode matter.

`select(FH)` returns the PREVIOUS selection, and in perl that is a GLOB, which
stringifies package-QUALIFIED.  PCL returns the stored designator verbatim --
the bare handle NAME:

    open DUP, ">&", *STDERR;
    open my $dup2, ">&", *STDOUT;
    select(DUP)      perl 'main::STDOUT'      PCL 'main::STDOUT'   agree
    select($dup2)    perl 'main::DUP'         PCL 'DUP'            DIVERGE
    select(STDOUT)   perl 'GLOB(0x5f6c...)'   PCL 'GLOB(0x1)'      (a lexical
                                                    handle; addresses differ
                                                    on every run either way)

STDOUT agrees because `p-select`'s no-selection default is the literal string
"main::STDOUT"; every other bareword handle comes back unqualified.

The non-ASCII spelling adds a second layer: `select($dÃ¹p)` after `select(DÃP)`
answers `'dÃ¹p'` where perl says `'main::DÃP'` -- unqualified AND case-folded,
which is the #418 family reaching the handle NAME.

WHERE: `p-select` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~19367) returns
`(or *p-selected-out* "main::STDOUT")` unchanged.  Its own docstring says the
returned value must stay a designator `%p-resolve-fh` accepts -- which the
"main::STDOUT" default already is, so a `main::`-qualified NAME is acceptable
there; the qualification must use the package the handle lives in, not a
blanket `main::` (#491 canonicalised the registry to the UNQUALIFIED name, so
the package has to come from somewhere else).

WHAT IT COSTS: `t/uni/select.t` rows 2 and 4 (`is select($dÃ¹p), "main::DÃP"`).
The file's other two failing rows are its own TODOs ("Scalar filehandles not
yet clean").

RELATED: #491 (done) canonicalised the handle name at the Environment seam for
the open / print / readline sites; this is the RETURN site, which it did not
cover.
subject: select(FH) returns a bareword handle name UNQUALIFIED where perl stringifies the previous GLOB as main::NAME -- t/uni/select.t rows 2 and 4 (ASCII-probed)
